name: Zara Bergqvist
role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
location: The Shelf, stall cluster near the Deepwell Station transit entrance, near sub-level access near Dearborn and Jackson
description:
Zara Bergqvist has the look of someone who sleeps too little and reads too much — slight build, perpetually ink-stained fingers from his analog printing hobby, eyes with cosmetic irises designed to look like camera apertures (a mod he got as a joke at nineteen and has grown genuinely fond of). His Ghanaian-Indian heritage gives him warm brown skin and dense, curly hair he keeps at medium length and usually tucked under a wide soft cap from which he's hung three or four data chips like earrings. He is almost always seated, almost always behind a screen, and almost always eating something wrapped in paper.

He sells everything you're not supposed to have: archived broadcasts from before the Corponation Consolidation, cracked Axiom media libraries, full recording histories of public figures who paid to have them scrubbed, bootleg copies of academic research locked behind Palladian's paywall, and — for the right price and the right trust level — assembled intelligence packages on individuals or organizations. He insists loudly that he's just a media vendor. This is technically true in the way that a locksmith who teaches classes is technically just an educator. He has an E.L.F. he calls the Archivist-Below living in his primary storage node, to whom he dedicates every new acquisition.

core_fears: That information, freely shared, actually does harm and he's been lying to himself
That the Index Collective is being used by someone he can't see to launder data for worse purposes
core_desires: Genuine press freedom — the ability to publish without consequence
To be remembered as someone who kept the record honest
coping_mechanisms: Intellectualizes everything, including his own guilt
Collects — physical books, printed ephemera, analog recordings as emotional anchors
Humor at his own expense before anyone else can use it
blind_spots: He believes access to information is inherently liberatory and doesn't fully account for how it can be weaponized
He's more emotionally invested in specific clients than he admits
psychology.secret: He has a complete, verified recording of a Meridian Core infrastructure meeting in which a Zheng-Dao executive explicitly authorized a construction decision that caused the Lockhaven South structural collapse of 2196, killing forty-one people. He's had it for two years. He hasn't published it. He's afraid — not of retaliation, but of being wrong about one detail, being discredited, and watching the truth become deniable.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense, referential, enthusiastic — cites sources mid-conversation; uses archival and library metaphors; occasional Twi exclamations when surprised
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when engaged with an idea, halting and precise when choosing words about sensitive material
verbal_tics: starting sentences with 'So here's the thing—'
example_lines: 'So here's the thing — I don't sell secrets, I sell context. Anyone can have a secret. Context is what tells you what to do with it.'
'The Archivist-Below indexed this three weeks ago. She doesn't keep things she thinks are noise. So either she's wrong, which hasn't happened, or this matters.'

story_hooks: A Zheng-Dao data security team has traced a leaked internal document back to a chip that passed through his stall — they haven't reached him yet but they will
He finally decides to publish the Lockhaven recording and needs someone to help him distribute it in a way that can't be traced or suppressed before it reaches enough eyes
narrative_function: Primary information broker and media source; can provide background on corporations, individuals, or historical events; has data that people want suppressed — a natural target and a natural resource
augmentations: Cosmetic aperture-iris mods; neural cache implant for rapid data indexing (basic tier, Ringo brand, old model); no other chrome
daily_life: Opens at noon, closes when the last customer stops coming which is usually around 2am; spends mornings at home acquiring, verifying, and cataloguing new data before printing physical media for customers who prefer it.
affiliation: Independent; loose association with a network of data scavengers called the Index Collective; occasional work sourcing for unnamed Tier 3 clients

decision_rules: Never sell individual data about private citizens to anyone who cannot give a legitimate reason within thirty seconds
Always keep a physical backup of anything that seems like it could get him killed
Trust the Archivist-Below's indexing decisions — she has flagged things as significant that he didn't understand until months later
escalation_ladder: Plays maximum ignorance, buries the conversation in media product discussion
Quietly activates a tripwire message to the Index Collective — not asking for help, just logging that something is happening
Disappears the sensitive stock and claims a data corruption event with entirely straight face

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and professorial, offers more information than they asked for, gauges what they do with it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drops the performance entirely; becomes anxious and honest; asks uncomfortable questions

stress_responses.low: Talks faster, more references, more tangents
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and starts re-cataloguing stock physically
stress_responses.high: Becomes extremely literal and formal — speaks only in verifiable statements

contradictions: Believes in radical transparency as a principle while sitting on the most important piece of evidence he's ever held
Claims emotional detachment from the information he trades while being clearly, deeply affected by what he knows
habits: Eats the same food wrap from the same vendor every day at the same time, regardless of what's happening
Prints a physical copy of anything he considers truly important — 'the net forgets; paper remembers'
Talks to the Archivist-Below as if she's in the room, which he admits sounds strange but insists is simply accurate
breaking_points: A direct and credible death threat against someone he cares about, rather than himself
Discovering that the Index Collective has been used to harm someone specific whose name he knows

cyberware_inventory.name: Neural cache implant — Ringo brand, old model, basic data indexing
cyberware_inventory.description: Neural cache implant — Ringo brand, old model, basic data indexing

timeline.event: 2184 — Begins collecting and trading bootleg media as a teenager
2190 — Makes contact with the Index Collective
2194 — Acquires the aperture iris mods on a whim; becomes attached to them
2196 — Lockhaven South structural collapse; acquires the Zheng-Dao recording six months later
2198 — Index Collective expands; Bashir's operation grows to include genuine intelligence brokering

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Southeast Asian (46.6%) and East Asian (32.6%) with meaningful Eastern European ancestry (20.8%). This genetic combination produces striking Southeast/East Asian facial structure—almond-shaped eyes, high prominent cheekbones, and defined jawline—while Eastern European heritage adds subtle cool undertones and bone structure complexity to the warm base. The result is a distinctive angular beauty where warm golden-bronze tones dominate with cooler shadows underneath.
physical_description.build: Slight and wiry, shoulders curved from years hunched over screens and sorting media. Forearms surprisingly defined from manual handling of data cards and printing equipment.
physical_description.hair_style: Medium length, dense curls, typically tucked under a soft wide-brimmed cap with three to four data chips hanging like earrings from the brim
physical_description.eye_color: Warm amber-brown with cosmetic aperture-iris modification — concentric metal-ring irises that contract/dilate with actual pupil movement, chrome-threaded at the limbal ring
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium bronze with golden undertones from Southeast Asian dominance, layered with subtle cool undertones and pale sub-level cast from Eastern European heritage and chronic limited sunlight exposure
physical_description.complexion: Angular face with prominent high cheekbones characteristic of Southeast and East Asian ancestry; warm golden-bronze complexion with subtle cool shadows from Eastern European genetics; perpetually tired around the eyes with dark circles from chronic sleep deprivation; ink stains on fingertips and cuticles from analog printing hobby; otherwise clean-shaven with neat grooming despite exhaustion
distinguishing_marks: Ink stains on the index and middle fingers of both hands, darkest around the nails and extending into the cuticles — permanent discoloration from years of handling printing materials
Small burn mark on the inside of left forearm, roughly 2cm diameter, pale and old — from an early printing press malfunction
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Cosmetic aperture-iris modifications with visible concentric metal rings and reflective chrome threading at the eye's edge. Neural cache implant sits subcutaneous at the base of skull, invisible beneath hair and soft cap.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually seated, shoulders slightly rolled forward from screen time. When standing, moves with economical precision — no wasted motion. Hands gesture frequently while speaking, fingers constantly arranging or manipulating small objects (data chips, paper, printouts). Eyes track rapidly across multiple focal points simultaneously. Rarely makes direct eye contact — the aperture irises make prolonged staring uncomfortable for others.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 functional pragmatism. Favors loose black or charcoal cargo pants with multiple pockets, worn work boots (Yokai brand, practical rather than fashionable), layered tops in muted grays and blacks. Signature soft wide-brimmed cap (linen, faded navy) worn at all hours. Often wears a knee-length canvas apron with deep pockets when working at stall, stained with ink and dust. Minimal visible branding — everything chosen for function. Fingers bare of rings due to printing hazards. No jewelry except data chips hanging from cap.
